title: Integral cubical lattice chains retract onto the augmentation
statement:
For an integer $r\geq0$ put $D=\mathbf Z^r$, with standard basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. For $0\leq a\leq r$ let $C_a$ be the free abelian group [def-weil-pbc-free-module] on symbols $[v,I]$ with $v\in D$ and $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of cardinality $a$, and put $C_a=0$ otherwise. Define
$$\partial_a[v,I]=\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^{\#\{j\in I:j<i\}}\bigl([v+u_i,I\setminus\{i\}]-[v,I\setminus\{i\}]\bigr),\qquad a\geq1.$$
Let $\epsilon:C_0\to\mathbf Z$ send every $[v,\varnothing]$ to $1$, let $s:\mathbf Z\to C_0$ send $1$ to $[0,\varnothing]$, and let $e:C_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ equal $s\epsilon$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere. Then $\partial_{a-1}\partial_a=0$, $\epsilon\partial_1=0$, and there are abelian-group homomorphisms $h_a:C_a\to C_{a+1}$ with
$$\partial_{a+1}h_a+h_{a-1}\partial_a=1-e_a\quad(a\geq0),\qquad \epsilon s=1,$$
where $h_{-1}\partial_0=0$. In particular $C_\bullet\xrightarrow{\epsilon}\mathbf Z$ is exact as an augmented chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Translation $w[v,I]=[v+w,I]$ commutes with $\partial$ and $\epsilon$ (with trivial action on $\mathbf Z$); each $C_a$ is a finite direct sum of copies of the free integral $D$-module on $D$, one for each $I$ of size $a$. The maps $h_a$ and $s$ need not commute with translation. For $r=0$ take $s=\epsilon=1$ and $h=0$.

proof.text: By the basis description in [def-weil-pbc-free-module], a prescribed finite integral combination for each $[v,I]$ extends uniquely to a homomorphism. Use this throughout. Put $\partial_0=0$. For distinct $i,j\in I$, removing $i$ then $j$ and removing $j$ then $i$ produce opposite signs: if $i<j$, their exponents are $q_i+q_j-1$ and $q_j+q_i$, where $q_k=\#\{l\in I:l<k\}$. Their four translated terms agree because translations in distinct coordinates commute. Pairing these terms gives $\partial^2=0$; degrees with fewer than two coordinates give zero directly. Also $\epsilon\partial_1[v,\{i\}]=1-1=0$. Thus these maps form the chain complex of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] with the stated augmentation.

proof.text: For $1\leq i\leq r$ let $\rho_i(v)=v-v_i u_i$, and define a degree-preserving homomorphism $p_i$ by $p_i[v,I]=0$ if $i\in I$, and $p_i[v,I]=[\rho_i(v),I]$ otherwise. If $i\notin I$, each face removes $j\ne i$ and $\rho_i(v+u_j)=\rho_i(v)+u_j$, so $p_i\partial=\partial p_i$. If $i\in I$, every face except the $i$-face is killed by $p_i$, while the two vertices of the $i$-face acquire the same $i$-coordinate zero and cancel. Hence $p_i$ is a chain map. The $p_i$ commute: each either kills a cell containing its coordinate, or resets that coordinate, independently of all others.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding displayed alternating differential, for comparison only; the following signed-coordinate construction and its verification are agent-written, not asserted by Tags 0623 or 062F.

proof.text: For any integer-indexed family $b(k)$ in an abelian group write $\Sigma_n b=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}b(k)$ for $n>0$, $\Sigma_0 b=0$, and $\Sigma_n b=-\sum_{k=n}^{-1}b(k)$ for $n<0$. Cancelling consecutive terms gives, for every integer $n$, $\Sigma_n(b(k+1)-b(k))=b(n)-b(0)$ and $\Sigma_{n+1}b-\Sigma_n b=b(n)$; these formulas include $n=-1,0$. For $i\notin I$ define the degree-one homomorphism $$H_i[v,I]=(-1)^{q_i}\Sigma_{v_i}\bigl[\rho_i(v)+ku_i,I\cup\{i\}\bigr],\qquad q_i=\#\{j\in I:j<i\},$$ and set $H_i[v,I]=0$ for $i\in I$. Every sum is finite, so this is a well-defined homomorphism by [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. It vanishes on $C_r$ and on degrees outside the stated range.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding displayed alternating differential, for comparison only; the following signed-coordinate construction and its verification are agent-written, not asserted by Tags 0623 or 062F.

proof.text: Suppose $i\notin I$. In $\partial H_i[v,I]$, the $i$-face has sign $(-1)^{q_i}$ as well as the prefactor $(-1)^{q_i}$. Its signed sum therefore telescopes to $[v,I]-[\rho_i(v),I]$. For $j\in I$, the other face terms cancel those of $H_i\partial[v,I]$, with identical bases and summation ranges. Indeed if $j<i$, their exponents are $q_i+q_j$ and $q_j+q_i-1$; if $j>i$, they are $q_i+q_j+1$ and $q_j+q_i$. Shifting in the $j$-direction leaves $v_i$ unchanged, so this compares the actual summands also for negative $v_i$. Thus $(\partial H_i+H_i\partial)[v,I]=(1-p_i)[v,I]$ when $i\notin I$.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding displayed alternating differential, for comparison only; the following signed-coordinate construction and its verification are agent-written, not asserted by Tags 0623 or 062F.

proof.text: Suppose $i\in I$. Here $H_i[v,I]=0$. In $H_i\partial[v,I]$ all faces except the $i$-face still contain $i$ and give zero. For that face the boundary and insertion signs are both $(-1)^{q_i}$, so their product is $1$. The two path sums have the same base $\rho_i(v)$ and upper endpoints $v_i+1$ and $v_i$. Their difference is exactly $[v,I]$ by $\Sigma_{v_i+1}-\Sigma_{v_i}$. Since $p_i[v,I]=0$, this proves $\partial H_i+H_i\partial=1-p_i$ on the remaining basis elements. Linearity gives this identity in every degree, including the top degree.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding displayed alternating differential, for comparison only; the following signed-coordinate construction and its verification are agent-written, not asserted by Tags 0623 or 062F.

proof.text: Put $P_0=1$ and $P_i=p_1\cdots p_i$, and in each degree set $h=\sum_{i=1}^r P_{i-1}H_i$. Every $P_i$ is a chain map by step 2, so the identities of steps 4 and 5 yield $$\partial h+h\partial=\sum_{i=1}^r P_{i-1}(1-p_i)=\sum_{i=1}^r(P_{i-1}-P_i)=1-P_r.$$ For $I\ne\varnothing$ one factor $p_i$ kills $[v,I]$, hence $P_r=0$ in positive degree; in degree zero it resets all coordinates and sends $[v,\varnothing]$ to $[0,\varnothing]$. Thus $P_r=e$ and the required contraction identity holds, with the degree-minus-one term zero. Directly $\epsilon s(1)=1$.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding displayed alternating differential, for comparison only; the following signed-coordinate construction and its verification are agent-written, not asserted by Tags 0623 or 062F.

proof.text: For $a>0$ and $x\in C_a$ with $\partial_a x=0$, the contraction gives $x=\partial_{a+1}h_a x$, proving exactness in positive degree. If $x\in C_0$ and $\epsilon x=0$, it gives $x=\partial_1 h_0x$; the opposite inclusion follows from $\epsilon\partial_1=0$. Surjectivity at $\mathbf Z$ follows from $\epsilon s=1$. These are precisely kernel equals image at every position of the augmented complex, or vanishing homology by [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. For $r=0$ there is just the basis vector $[0,\varnothing]$; identify its group with $\mathbf Z$. The empty sum gives $h=0$ and the augmentation and section are identities.

proof.text: For $w\in D$, replacing $v$ by $v+w$ in each summand of $\partial[v,I]$ gives exactly $w\partial[v,I]$; also $\epsilon[v+w,\varnothing]=1=\epsilon[v,\varnothing]$. Fixing $I$ of size $a$, the subgroup with basis $[v,I]$ is the free abelian group on $D$ with its translation action, i.e. the free integral $D$-module on one orbit. The basis partitions by $I$, so $C_a$ is the direct sum of these subgroups by [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. There are finitely many such subsets of the finite set $\{1,\ldots,r\}$. No equivariance of $h$ or $s$ was used or claimed: for $r=1$, $s(1)=[0,\varnothing]$ already fails to be fixed by translation by $u_1$.
